title: Ordinary scalar evaluation and its unit tensor map
statement: For a site with sheafified modules, let E_a be actual additive scalar extensions along all maps of commutative ring sheaves, with their ordinary scalar adjunctions, specified object/map equations and scalar-unit normalization [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data]. Suppose strong chain tensor comparisons send each unit of x tensor p to the tensor of the units of x and p. There are normalized maps nu_a:S tensor_R D -> UE_aD, chain evaluations ev_b:D tensor_R P -> I, scalar evaluations h_b:(S tensor_R D) tensor_R P -> UE_aI and unit tensor maps UE_aD tensor_R P -> U(E_aD tensor_S E_aP), with formulas nu(s tensor x)=s tensor x, ev_b(x tensor p)=b(x)(p), h_b((s tensor x) tensor p)=s tensor b(x)(p), and y tensor p -> y tensor (1 tensor p). All inputs are arbitrary complexes. The ordinary extensions have a strict chain presentation and compatible strict squares for each commuting coefficient square [lem-sfb-hom-scalar-chain-identification] [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. Neither derived-category choices nor flatness hypotheses occur.

proof.text: Compare ordinary extensions by the specified object and map equations. Map the comparison to complexes. The ordinary unit equation proves its generator normalization. Compose the canonical strict nu with this comparison to obtain nu and the strict presentation.

Use ordinary chain tensor-Hom transposition to construct evaluation. Compose the ordinary scalar adjunction unit, chain tensor comparison and counit to construct the unit tensor map. The triangle identity proves its generator formula.

Compose nu, the unit tensor map, inverse tensor comparison and extended evaluation to construct scalar evaluation. The inverse tensor comparison sends (s tensor x) tensor (1 tensor p) to s tensor (x tensor p), by linearity and its normalized unit equation. The previous formulas give s tensor b(x)(p). The canonical strict coefficient squares and their proved compatibility supply all coefficient-square data.
